newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures fall near limit, then recover.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures fall near limit, then recover.

text.p: CME lumber futures fell for a near limit loss of $9.20 per thousand board feet in March on profit taking before finding support and paring losses, traders said.
At 0927 CST, lumber stood $5.70 to $3.00 lower with March off most at $430.00 per tbf and May off $3.70 at $393.50.

Profit taking was evident from the start following a recent two-day rally in prices to new contract highs. Reported higher cash lumber prices were already in the market. A break in financials late Thurday and weak financial markets early Friday also weighed on sentiment before support was uncovered at the lower price level, traders said.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $413 per tbf, up $10 from Wednesday and up $17 from last Friday. Improving weather, especially in the East, offset the weak home building trend in December due to harsh winter weather.
